  "text": "Ruth brought the curtains down in a carrier bag. Her mother had folded them around the hooks.

“Careful,” she said. “They catch.”

The laundrette was between a bakery and an empty shop. Ruth held the door while her mother carried the bag through sideways.

“I could have managed these in the bath.”

“And got them dry where?”

Her mother inspected the machines without answering.

They chose the largest one. Ruth fed coins into the slot while her mother watched each disappear.

“It used to be half that.”

“It used to be smaller curtains.”

“They’re the same curtains.”

Ruth pressed the button.

For a while they sat beneath a notice asking customers not to wash horse blankets. Her mother kept her handbag on her knees.

“Coffee?” Ruth asked.

“Not from a machine.”

“There’s the bakery.”

“Then yes.”

When Ruth returned, her mother had moved two chairs closer to the washer.

“So nobody takes them,” she said.

Ruth handed her a paper cup and a small bag.

“I didn’t ask for a bun.”

“They had the ones with cherries.”

Her mother opened the bag.

The curtains tumbled past the round window, briefly showing the faded strip that had faced the garden for twenty years.

“I might turn them,” her mother said.

“They’ll look different.”

“Only to me.”

After drying, they folded them on the long table. Ruth took one end and waited while her mother matched the corners.

“You’ll come up?” her mother asked.

“To hang them, yes.”

“I meant for lunch.”

Ruth lifted the bag.

“What have you got?”

“Enough,” her mother said, and checked beneath their chairs before they left."
